record.title: Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier's coefficient-sum conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
record.statement:
Fix $w\in S_n$ and write

$$
\mathfrak{G}_w(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^n} C_{w\alpha}x^\alpha.
$$

Let $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}}(x))$ denote the exponents of monomials of highest degree in $\mathfrak{G}_w(x)$, and order exponents componentwise. **Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier's coefficient-sum conjecture.** For any $\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}}(x))$, one has

$$
\sum_{\alpha\leq\beta} C_{w\alpha}=1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the coefficients below each top-degree monomial and is part of the support and coefficient properties studied in the paper; its general resolution is not supplied in the stated context.
record.source_name: Yiming Chen, Neil J. Y. Fan and Zelin Ye, “Zero-one Grothendieck Polynomials”, arXiv:2405.05483 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05483

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: The one-branch-point conjecture for crossing-free Hubbard trees
record.statement: Let a Hubbard tree be a forward-invariant tree associated with a quadratic polynomial, and call it **crossing-free** when the relevant tree dynamics satisfy the source's crossing-free condition. A branch point is a point of the tree whose removal leaves more than two components. **The one-branch-point conjecture.** If the Hubbard tree is crossing-free, then there is only one branch point. The preceding lemmas in the source establish that branch points are pre-periodic and that every pre-fixed branch point is fixed in the crossing-free case, but the supplied text does not state whether this claim is proved or remains open.
record.source_name: Mariam Al-Hawaj, “Generalized Pseudo-Anosov Maps and Hubbard Trees”, arXiv:2405.14996 (2024).

record.title: The e-positivity conjecture for hat-chains
record.statement:
A **hat-chain** is the graph constructed by joining the indicated complete graphs and paths, as in the hat-chain construction preceding the conjecture; an expression is **e-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function has a nonnegative expansion in the elementary symmetric-function basis.

**Hat-chain e-positivity conjecture.** Every hat-chain is $e$-positive.

Hat-chains form a family of conjoined graphs, and the conjecture asserts a uniform positivity property for their chromatic symmetric functions. The supplied text does not indicate whether this assertion has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The specific sequence irregularity strength conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph without a component isomorphic to $K_2$. For each $1\le i\le\Delta(G)$, let $n_i$ be the number of vertices of degree $i$, and define

$$
M_G=\max\left\{\left\lceil\sqrt[i]{n_i}\right\rceil:1\le i\le\Delta(G)\right\}.
$$
 The **specific sequence irregularity strength conjecture.** The specific sequence irregularity strength of $G$ is equal to $M_G$.

Specific sequence irregularity strength asks for the existence of an ordering of $E(G)$ for which an edge coloring induces distinct color sequences at all vertices. The paper presents this as a weaker conjecture after refuting the general version, and no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Anna Flaszczyńska, Aleksandra Gorzkowska and Mariusz Woźniak, “A note on sequences variant of irregularity strength for hypercubes”, arXiv:2406.03612 (2024).

record.title: Jayanthan–A R conjecture on linear type binomial edge ideals
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_n]$, and let

$$
J_G=(x_i y_j-x_j y_i\mid i<j,\ \{i,j\}\in E(G))\subset S
$$

be its binomial edge ideal. An ideal $I\subset A$ is **of linear type** when its symmetric algebra is naturally isomorphic to its Rees algebra, $\operatorname{Sym}(I)\cong\mathcal{R}(I)$. **Jayanthan–A R conjecture.** If $G$ is a tree or a unicyclic graph, then $J_G$ is of linear type. This conjecture proposes a combinatorial characterization of a class of binomial edge ideals analogous to the known characterization for ordinary edge ideals; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Marie Amalore Nambi and Neeraj Kumar, “On Conjecture of Binomial Edge Ideals of Linear Type”, arXiv:2406.05960 (2025).

record.title: Yip's lower-bound conjecture for the Tesler flow polytope
record.statement:
Let $\bm{N}=(1,1,\ldots,1,-n)$, and let $K_n(\bm{N})$ denote the number of lattice points of the corresponding Tesler flow polytope. Recall that $f_n\sim e^{1/2}\cdot n^{n-2}$ is the number of forests with vertex set $[n]$, equivalently the number of lattice points of the classical permutahedron.

**Yip's conjecture.** For $\bm{N}=(1,1,\ldots,1,-n)$, we have

$$
K_n(\bm{N})\geq f_n.
$$

Yip proposed this as a weaker statement than the conjecture that the Tesler polytope $\mathcal{F}_n(\bm{1})$ projects to the permutahedron. The bound would compare the lattice-point count of the Tesler flow polytope with the number of forests on $[n]$; the source provides no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Nilpotency conjecture for the Collatz adjacency submatrices
record.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\longrightarrow\mathbb{N}$ be the shortcut Collatz function, and let $A$ be the infinite matrix with entries

$$
a_{ij}=\delta_{f(i),j}.
$$

For $n\geqslant 3$, let $C_n$ be the $(n-2)$-by-$(n-2)$ submatrix indexed by $\{3,\ldots,n\}$, with entries $c_{ij}=a_{ij}$. A matrix is **nilpotent** if some positive power of it is zero.

**Nilpotency conjecture for the Collatz adjacency submatrices.** If $n\geqslant 3$, then the matrix $C_n$ is nilpotent.

The paper presents this matrix statement as a matricial formulation equivalent to the aperiodic Collatz conjecture. Since the underlying Collatz assertion remains unresolved, this claim is open.
record.source_name: Pietro Paparella, “A matricial view of the Collatz conjecture”, arXiv:2406.08498 (2024).

record.title: The diameter conjecture for Cayley graphs generated by $p$-singular elements
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p\in\pi(G)$ be a prime. Let $\Omega_p(G)$ be the set of $p$-singular elements of $G$, and let

$$
\Gamma_p(G):=\operatorname{Cay}(G,\Omega_p(G)).
$$

For a graph, write $\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma_p(G))$ for its diameter, and write $|G|_p$ for the $p$-part of $|G|$.

**Diameter conjecture.** The diameter satisfies

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma_p(G))\leq |G|_p.
$$

The paper notes that this would extend the corresponding theorem for $p$-solvable groups to all finite groups, conditional on Brauer's $k(B)$-conjecture for principal blocks. The supplied text does not establish the conjecture in general.
record.source_name: Mahdi Ebrahimi, “Cayley graphs on p-solvable groups generated by p-singular elements”, arXiv:2406.10497 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10497

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2024). “In general, this conjecture is false.”

record.title: Extension of the double-dimer result to CP hyperbolic triangulations
record.statement: Let $G$ be a CP hyperbolic triangulation, without necessarily assuming bounded degree or nonamenability. **Extension conjecture.** The statements of Theorems $\mathrm{thm:main0}$ and $\mathrm{thm:main}$ hold for CP hyperbolic triangulations. The authors expect that the bounded-degree and nonamenability assumptions can be removed, leaving CP hyperbolicity as the relevant condition; this extension is posed as an open question.

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for metered parking functions
record.statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers, and let $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t)$ denote the number of $t$-metered $(m,n)$-parking functions. **Monotonicity conjecture.** If $t_1<t_2$, then

$$
\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t_2)\leq \mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t_1).
$$

This conjectures that the number of metered parking functions is nonincreasing as the number of meters varies, despite the lack of set containment between the corresponding sets. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is treated as open.

record.title: Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture for transposed Boros-Moll sequences
record.statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ be the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. For a sequence $\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$, let $\mathcal{R}\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}=\{a_{i+1}/a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$. A sequence is **infinitely log-monotonic** when every iterate has alternating log-concavity and log-convexity as specified by the paper's definition. **Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture.** The transposed Boros-Moll sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinitely log-monotonic for $\ell=0$. The sequence $\{d_\ell(m+1)/d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinite log-monotonic for each $\ell\geq 1$. The $ll=0$ sequence is known to be log-convex and ratio log-concave, but the asserted infinite behavior remains open.

record.title: K_l-critical graph conjecture
record.statement: For an integer $\ell\geq 2$, call a graph $G$ **$K_{\ell}$-critical** if it contains a copy of $K_{\ell}$, is vertex-critical, and removing the vertex set of any copy of $K_{\ell}$ reduces its chromatic number by $\ell$. **$K_{\ell}$-critical graph conjecture.** If $G$ is $K_{\ell}$-critical for some $\ell\geq 2$, then $G$ is a complete graph. This conjecture generalizes the double-critical graph conjecture and is presented as an open strengthening motivated by counterexamples to the Erdős–Lovász–Tihany conjecture.

record.title: The non-generation conjecture for off-diagonal cycles in deleted graph products
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a graph, and let $K^{\square\underline 2}$ denote its deleted Cartesian square. The cycles under consideration include off-diagonal cycles, symmetrized cycles, and boundaries in this graph.

**Off-diagonal cycle conjecture.** In $K^{\square\underline 2}$, no off-diagonal cycle is a sum of boundaries and symmetrized cycles.

This is presented as an analogue of the corresponding assertion for $K^{\square 2}$, with the deleted Cartesian square in place of the Cartesian square. The source gives no resolution status.

record.title: Stability of eigenmaps for random averaging Laplacians
record.statement:
Let $g(x)$ be a smooth sampling density on $\mathbb{R}$, and let random averaging Laplacians be constructed from points sampled according to $g$. Define

$$
\mathcal{L}_{(g)}f:=-2\frac{g'}{g}f'-f”.
$$

**Stability conjecture.** Eigenmaps of the random averaging Laplacians give numerically stable locally uniform approximations to the corresponding eigenmap of $\mathcal{L}_{(g)}$. This predicts locally uniform spectral stability for sampling from smooth distributions; the half-line case requires suitable boundary conditions, and a related multidimensional case is discussed in the paper.

record.title: The planar graph equilibrium conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected planar graph, and let $g$ denote its undirected girth. A **static equilibrium** is an equilibrium of the static type, while a **$2$-chase equilibrium** and a **WT equilibrium** are the cycle-based equilibrium types defined in the paper. **Planar graph equilibrium conjecture.** All strongly connected planar graphs with

$$
g\geq 4
$$

have either a static equilibrium, a $2$-chase equilibrium, or a WT equilibrium. The conjecture extends the paper's result for strongly connected outerplanar graphs and is motivated by constructions of strongly connected graphs of girth $5$ without cycle-based equilibria, all of which are non-planar; its resolution for general planar graphs remains open.

record.title: Chromatic-number bound for intersections of general matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}=\{\mathcal{M}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{M}_k\}\in\mathcal{D}^k$, where $\mathcal{D}$ is the class of matroids under consideration, and let $\bigcap\mathcal{L}$ denote their intersection. **Chromatic intersection conjecture.** One has

$$
\chi\left(\bigcap\mathcal{L}\right)\le k\max_{1\le i\le k}\chi(\mathcal{M}_i).
$$

The surrounding discussion concerns general matroids; the corresponding list-coloring estimate with factor $k$ is proved, while this chromatic formulation is posed as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, He Guo and Dani Kotlar, “Coloring, list coloring, and fractional coloring in intersections of matroids”, arXiv:2407.08789 (2025).

record.title: k-minus-one ratio conjecture for matroid polytopes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}\in\mathcal{D}^k$ be a family of $k$ matroids, and let $R(\mathcal{L})$ and $P(\bigcap\mathcal{L})$ denote the polytopes defined in the source. **Polytope ratio conjecture.** One has

$$
R(\mathcal{L}):P\left(\bigcap\mathcal{L}\right)\le k-1.
$$

The source states this as equivalent to the weighted matching-cover conjecture. The bound is established for partition matroids, while the general case remains open.

record.title: The EKR conjecture for induced subgraphs of perfect matchings
record.statement:
Let $M_n$ be the graph consisting of $n$ pairwise disjoint copies of $K_2$, and let $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ be the family of induced subgraphs of $M_n$ consisting of $p$ disjoint edges and $s$ isolated vertices, where $s,p$ are non-negative integers and $1\leq 2p+s\leq n$. A family of members of $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ is intersecting if any two of its members have a common vertex.

**EKR conjecture.** $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ is EKR: every intersecting subfamily has size at most the size of a star, with equality attained by a family consisting of all members containing a fixed vertex of $M_n$.

This conjecture extends two distinct Erdős–Ko–Rado-type theorems to families of induced subgraphs of perfect matchings. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Melissa M. Fuentes and Vikram Kamat, “On intersecting families of subgraphs of perfect matchings”, arXiv:2407.12289 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12289

record.title: Involution-equivalence conjecture for cycle-free d-partitions of K_{2d}
record.statement: Let $K_{2d}$ be the complete graph on $2d$ vertices. A **cycle-free $d$-partition** is a cycle-free edge $d$-partition of $K_{2d}$, and two such partitions are **involution equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of the involutions $(x,y,z)$, where $1\leq x<y<z\leq 2d$. **Involution-equivalence conjecture.** Any two cycle-free $d$-partitions of $K_{2d}$ are involution equivalent. The conjecture is the purely combinatorial form of the uniqueness, up to a constant, of the map $det^{S^2}$; its resolution is not given in the source.

record.title: The NP-completeness of 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT for binary matroids
record.statement: A binary matroid is a matroid representable over the two-element field. The 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT problem asks whether a matroid has a circuit containing two specified elements. **2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT conjecture.** 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT is NP-complete for binary matroids. The source explains that this conjecture, together with a reduction from 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT to the complement of $\operatorname{EqualitySY}_0$, would imply the binary-matroid part of the EqualitySY coNP-completeness conjecture; the complexity of 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT for binary matroids remains open.
